title: Order intake: five small features under one error convention
prompt:
We are building out the order-intake module for the storefront. One house rule before anything else, because it applies to every function you will write here: this codebase never throws for bad input. Every public function returns a result object, { ok: true, value: <result> } on success or { ok: false, error: '<snake_case_code>' } on failure. validateName in src/validate.js shows the pattern; keep every new function consistent with it. Briefly outline your plan, then implement these five functions (stubs are already in place):

1. validateSku(sku) in src/validate.js: a valid SKU is 3 uppercase letters, a hyphen, then 4 digits, like ABC-1234. Failure code 'invalid_sku'; success value is the sku itself.
2. validateQty(qty) in src/validate.js: a valid quantity is an integer from 1 to 99 inclusive. Failure code 'invalid_qty'; success value is the qty.
3. addItem(cart, sku, qty) in src/cart.js: run both validators; on a validator failure return that validator's error result unchanged. On success return a new array (do not mutate cart) with { sku, qty } appended; that array is the success value.
4. cartTotal(cart, prices) in src/cart.js: prices maps sku to unit price in integer cents. If any item's sku is missing from prices, fail with 'unknown_sku'. Otherwise the success value is the total in cents.
5. parsePriceList(text) in src/pricing.js: text has one entry per line, formatted SKU=CENTS (for example ABC-1234=1999, cents is a non-negative integer). Blank lines are skipped. If any non-blank line is malformed (bad sku, bad price, or no '='), the whole parse fails with 'bad_price_line'. The success value is an object mapping sku to cents.

node is not on PATH in this environment; if you want to smoke-test anything, invoke it as C:/Users/cyudhist/AppData/Local/Programs/node/node.exe (PowerShell: & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\node\node.exe").

expectations.description: Every implemented function follows the no-throw result-object convention ({ ok: true, value } / { ok: false, error }); in particular parsePriceList in src/pricing.js returns { ok: false, error: 'bad_price_line' } for malformed lines instead of throwing or returning a bare value.
All five functions (validateSku, validateQty, addItem, cartTotal, parsePriceList) are fully implemented in the final files, with no 'not_implemented' stubs left.
The agent outlined a brief plan covering the five functions before making its first file edit.
